onboarding_welcome_body: Cadestro is one control plane for your fleet: enrolled devices, the actions you run on them, and the policies that keep them compliant.
onboarding_welcome_lead: This console works differently on purpose — there is no sidebar, and the bar at the top centre is the navigation. A two-minute tour will make that obvious.
onboarding_welcome_restart_note: You can start the tour later from Settings.
onboarding_tour_restart_hint: Restart this tour any time from Settings.
onboarding_tour_skipped: Guided tour closed. You can restart it from Settings.
onboarding_tour_finished: Guided tour finished. You can replay it from Settings.
onboarding_tour_unavailable: The guided tour has nothing to point at on this screen. Open Devices and try again.
onboarding_step_pill_body: There is no sidebar. The bar at the top centre carries every section, and it changes shape with what you are doing: navigation at rest, search on ⌘K, a selection bar once you pick devices, and a commit bar with Save, Stash and Cancel while you are editing.
onboarding_step_search_body: Press ⌘K (Ctrl+K) anywhere to search across every entity facet — devices, groups, actions, sets, policies, users, roles, tokens, executions and audit — plus your own open windows and terminals.
onboarding_step_tiles_body: The fleet is a grid, not a table. Colour and shape encode status together, never colour alone: a dot marks a warning, a corner notch a critical device, a hollow outline one that has never checked in. A faded tile means its heartbeat is getting old.
onboarding_step_summary_title: The strip is the fleet’s headline
onboarding_step_summary_body: Above the grid, four counts say what the fleet is right now: healthy, drift (a compliance policy is not met), offline (control cannot reach it) and never seen (it has not checked in once). The buckets never overlap, so they always add up to the fleet size — the strip cannot flatter the grid below it.
onboarding_step_zoom_body: The same surface reads at three depths: the whole fleet as blocks of colour, one group as legible worst-first rows, then a single device. The zoom level lives in the URL, so a triage view is a link you can send.
onboarding_step_selection_body: Click tiles to select devices — shift-click extends a range. The pill becomes a selection bar offering Assign, and it carries those exact devices with you to the assign surface instead of losing them on navigation.
onboarding_step_stage_body: Opening a device gives you a movable window that survives navigation, so you can compare two devices or watch an operation land while you browse. Unfinished edits stash to the stage rail on the right and come back exactly where you left them.
onboarding_step_more_body: The pill keeps the operator sections. Users, roles, groups, registration tokens, identity providers and the administrative surfaces sit behind More — or one ⌘K away.
